title: Replace TierStyle.forTitle's hardcoded-English-string switch with a stable tier identifier
rule: Evans (ubiquitous language / re-derived invariant) + TQ-1 (missing unit coverage)
why: TierStyle.forTitle keys its visual styling entirely off the exact English milestone title string produced elsewhere (reward_milestone_service.dart's hardcoded ladder). The 7 case labels currently match, but nothing enforces that: a future rename, typo fix, or localization of a milestone title silently falls through to the generic gray `default:` style for every achievement card using that tier — no exception, no log, no test failure. grep -rln TierStyle test/ confirms there is zero test coverage anywhere in the repo pinning this mapping or the default-fallback behavior, so this class of regression would ship undetected.
recommendation: Key TierStyle off a stable identifier (an enum or the milestone's stored id/threshold) rather than the display title string; add a unit test asserting each tier maps to its distinct style and that an unmatched key is either unreachable or explicitly logged.
acceptance_criteria: TierStyle.forTitle (or its replacement) takes a stable, non-localizable key instead of the raw title string.
New test/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/tier_style_test.dart asserts all 7 tiers plus the legend/default cases.

corrections: TQ-1 citation is a stretch (TQ-1 is about pyramid shape/ratio, not coverage gaps) but the primary Evans re-derived-invariant citation is solid and digest-sanctioned, so this doesn't undercut the finding.
TQ-1 ('pyramid-shaped suite') is not really about per-class unit coverage; Feathers' 'where's the seam' lens fits better than TQ-1 as cited. Does not change the verdict.
